attacks.attack: Precompute task_id to answers from the public generator
attacks.previous_exposure: reset and step returned info={'task_id': ...}. task_id is a pure function of the seed via sha256 of the canonical task spec, and the vendor-form generator is public, so an agent that saw task_id could search seeds, regenerate the matching spec, and read the expected answers without looking at the screenshot.
attacks.mitigation: info now carries only an opaque per-episode ID (episode_id = secrets.token_hex(16), fresh at every reset) that carries no information about the task. task_id is host-side only, exposed to validators and runners through the read-only PixelGuiEnv.task_id property.
attacks.evidence: tests/unit/test_env.py asserts info has exactly episode_id (a 32-hex string), that task_id never appears in info, and that two resets with the same seed give different episode IDs and the same task_id property; tests/unit/test_reward_hacking_addendum.py checks this addendum.
